literal: Killing-like harm even if [they] do, they did one good thing to think [of], [the harm] will perish.
translation: Even if someone does you a harm as grievous as murder, it will vanish from your mind when you remember a single good thing they have done for you.
modern: ஒருவர் நம்மைக் கொல்வது போன்ற பெருந்துன்பத்தைச் செய்தாலும், அவர் முன்பு செய்த ஒரு நன்மையை நினைத்துப் பார்த்தால் அந்தத் துன்பம் மறைந்துவிடும்.
explanation: This couplet emphasizes the power of gratitude to overcome resentment. The phrase 'கொன்றன்ன இன்னா' (harm like killing) sets up the extreme case of someone causing the worst possible pain. Yet, the poet says that even if they commit such an act, the pain 'கெடும்' (will perish or be erased). The condition for this erasure is simply 'உள்ள' (to remember) just 'ஒன்று நன்று' (one good thing) that the same person did in the past. By focusing on a single past kindness, the mind lets go of even the most severe present injury.
